paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Worship didn't end when the Israelites left Jerusalem. They went out and kept going until the pillars, poles, high places and altars were utterly destroyed (2 Chronicles 31:1). I think that's a good question for any of us: what does our worship do once we walk out the door?

Now look at Hezekiah. He doesn't only give orders. He gives from his own possessions for the offerings (2 Chronicles 31:3), and he commands the people to give so the priests and Levites can devote themselves to the Law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 31:4). The people give generously (2 Chronicles 31:5), and Azariah, the chief priest, tells the king, "…the LORD has blessed His people; this great abundance is what is left over" (2 Chronicles 31:10). In this passage, when God's people gave, the priests had enough to eat with plenty left over, and Azariah points to the LORD's blessing.

The writer sums it up this way: Hezekiah "did what was good and upright and true before the LORD his God" (2 Chronicles 31:20). He "acted with all his heart in every work that he began in the service of the house of God… in order to seek his God" (2 Chronicles 31:21). So here's my question for you, baker. What's one thing you could do with ALL your heart this week, to seek God? Do that one, and leave the rest to Him.
